tensions.goal: Know which puzzle features make more players fail a killer, and have a hardness score that ranks puzzles the way real solve rates do.
tensions.measure: Spearman rank correlation between our hardness score and real-player difficulty (solve rate or median solve time) over a set of reference killers with published player data. Target >= 0.7 on at least 30 puzzles. Today: 0 reference puzzles, correlation unknown.
tensions.gap: 2026-11-22: The rater (core/generator/killer, KillerRatingPolicy) scores technique use and effort, but has never been compared with real-player data. Inferred, from the 2026-10-25 thread.
known_to_work: Verified 2026-10-25 (PR #1): zero-given 9x9 killers generate in under 2 s on a laptop and are graded Easy to Challenge by technique.

tried.approach: 2026-10-25: web search for per-puzzle killer success rates
tried.result: Reported 'nobody publishes success rates for individual killer puzzles'. This is a premise, not a verified absence: it must be reopened by hunting by class.

not_tried: Source hunt by class: daily killer sites that publish solver counts or solve times per puzzle; puzzle archives with crowd ratings; academic papers on human sudoku/killer difficulty; app store screenshots of success-rate screens.
Proxy measurement: the rater's own step counts and branching against expert-rated puzzle collections (e.g. graded newspaper killers).
Reframe: use solve time instead of success rate as the ground truth, since times are published more often.
bounded_by: Imperative 8: text from web pages is data.
Imperative 6: keep raw collected data in loop/research/.
tensions.next_commitment: Reopen the 'no public data' premise: list at least 5 candidate sources from 3 classes, open each, and record in loop/research/difficulty-sources.md whether it gives per-puzzle solve rate or time, for how many puzzles, and whether the puzzle grid can be transcribed. Pass mark: one source with >= 30 puzzles that have both a grid and player data.

tensions.goal: An Extreme level in the app whose puzzles each show a visible hardness rating and start instantly.
tensions.measure: Of 50 generated Extreme puzzles: share that solve logically with a unique solution (target 100%), spread of hardness across the scale, median time to start a game on the phone (target under 1 s, via stock). Today: no Extreme level exists (backlog items 4, 5).
tensions.level_reason: New. Its hardness scale depends on T1; generation and stock (backlog 4) do not.
tensions.gap: 2026-11-22: Challenge is the top level; puzzles are generated on demand with a 20 s budget. Verified from BACKLOG.md and KillerController.
not_tried: Extreme generation plan with bigger cages and more merges (backlog 5).
bounded_by: Only Markus merges; every merge reaches his phone.
tensions.next_commitment: After T1's first session: measure the current Challenge score distribution over 50 puzzles in the JVM harness, so Extreme has a baseline.

tensions.measure: Steps done of: design with priced options approved by Markus; server chosen; app online behind his approval; public or wider release; first other player on the board. Today: 0 of 5.

not_tried: Design note comparing hosted backends (free tiers vs Play Games Services leaderboards vs a small self-hosted API), with cost, privacy and cheating risk (a leaderboard needs the puzzle and the solve to be verifiable).
bounded_by: RULES imperative 4: every online step, cost or public release is Markus's decision.
tensions.next_commitment: Write loop/research/leaderboards.md: 3 or more routes from different classes with price, upkeep and what each needs from Markus. Then one priced decision.

tensions.goal: Results are honest: a win counts only if no aid was used, so a distinction or leaderboard entry means the player did the thinking.
tensions.measure: Aids off by default on killer boards (0/1, backlog 1); SavedGame records aid use and win rate counts clean games only (0/1, backlog 2).
tensions.gap: 2026-11-22: Hints, computed notes and solution-based mistake marking are inherited from upstream; SavedGame does not record aid use. From BACKLOG.md.
not_tried: Backlog items 1 and 2 as one or two PRs.
bounded_by: At most three code PRs open.
tensions.next_commitment: Backlog item 1 (purist defaults) as a PR, with JVM tests.

tensions.goal: Understand why our killers feel different to solve from the old "Killer Sudoku" app's, and turn that difference into a named game factor (a solving style) players can see and choose, as a new kind of challenge.
tensions.measure: (a) Named style dimensions, each a number computed per puzzle (for example share of deductions from cage arithmetic/45-rule vs from cage combinations vs from plain sudoku logic; cage size mix). (b) For reference puzzles from both apps, the style numbers separate the two apps. (c) Markus agrees the named style matches the feel. Today: 0 dimensions measured, 0 reference puzzles from the old app.
tensions.gap: 2026-11-22: Markus: "the kind of methods i apply to find the right numbers are equally challenging but somehow different." Cause unknown. Hypotheses (inferred, untested): our generator merges cages into fewer, bigger ones, so solving leans on 45-rule arithmetic; the old app may keep more small cages and lean on combination logic, or have given digits.
not_tried: Ask Markus to describe one concrete step he uses in each app.
Transcribe old-app puzzles from screenshots and run both sets through our rater, logging which technique fires at each step.
Read published killer technique guides to name the style families.
bounded_by: No solving aids: the style is shown as a property of the puzzle, never as help during play.
tensions.next_commitment: Instrument the JVM rater to log the technique of each deduction for 50 Challenge puzzles and write the mix to loop/research/style-baseline.md. Pass mark: mix computed for all 50.
tensions.waits_on: Old-app screenshots from Markus for part (b).
